messages:
maria: heads-up: after rolling v8.0 to canary pool A we see p99 token-latency jump ~45% and overall throughput drop ~18% :grimacing:

runtime-bot: alert: latency_spike detected on pool-A v8.0 (p99 tokens) — incident id inc-215123

aaron: seeing the same on our dashboards. Quick dump of batcher metrics shows average batch size down from 8->3 around the rollout window.

jasper: uploaded kvcache stats, look at evict_rate and hot_keys. evictions spiked at the same time as latency. snippet:
```
KVCache: hit_rate=0.87 -> 0.65
evict_rate=1200/s -> 4500/s
hot_keys=12 -> 78
```

leo: profiler results attached. interesting: kernel selector flipped from fast_attention_v3 to custom_seq_kernel_v1 for many allocations when avg_seq_len crossed ~240.
```
profile: kernel_choice: fast_attention_v3(60%) -> custom_seq_kernel_v1(70%)
seq_len_avg: 198 -> 262
```

maria: that smells like tokenizer change in v8.0 (we switched subtoken policy). Could be increasing effective sequence length and changing kernel heuristics.

jasper: batcher logs show hinting decided to reduce wait window because of tail latency—so it emitted smaller batches to keep per-request latency but that backfired due to throughput loss and more KV cache churn.
```
batcher: window_us=250 -> 80
batch_size_target=8 -> 3
```

ava: can we reproduce on canary host? I'll run a replay with traffic mix + tracing. Running `./tools/replay --pool A --model v8.0 --duration 10m` now.

leo: quick experiment: pinned kernel selector to prefer fast_attention_v3 on one canary box, latency went down ~22% (p99 improvement). That suggests kernel misselection + seq-len distribution causing runtime perf regression.

aaron: I also tried disabling prefetcher on a host (it was aggressively prefetching KV pages), that reduced evictions by ~35% and decreased p99 further.

maria: so hypothesis: tokenizer change in v8 bumped avg seq length -> kernel selector picks custom_seq_kernel_v1 (slower for our hardware/config) + prefetcher politeness combined with smaller batches -> KV churn and eviction -> higher tail latency.

jasper: logs for the moment of spike (from host 10.4.2.11):
```
[12:03:21] kernel_select: seq_len=256 -> chosen=custom_seq_kernel_v1
[12:03:21] kv_prefetch: enq 78 keys
[12:03:21] kv_evict: pressure=high
[12:03:22] batch_emit: size=2 (window=80us)
```

ava: I uploaded the flamegraph to the incident folder: https://redwood-internal/bridges/inc-215123/fg.html

leo: suggested mitigations: 1) immediate rollback of v8.0 canary (ops?) 2) add a soft threshold in kernel selector so small seq_len increases don't flip to slower kernel unless >10% tail impact 3) adjust batcher hinting to avoid shrinking window based on transient tail events 4) throttle prefetcher aggressiveness under high eviction rates.

deploy-bot: rollback scheduled for canary pool-A at 12:45 UTC as requested by @maria

maria: let's do the rollback ASAP and open a follow-up RFC for kernel selection heuristics + rollout checklist to include tokenization delta tests (sample seq-len distributions) before canary. Also add automated perf regression gates tied to p99 token latency + batch_size.

aaron: I'll make a quick patch to temporarily prefer fast_attention_v3 for v8.0 on pool-A so we can keep traffic while we validate changes.

jasper: after rollback + kernel pin on a few nodes we're back to pre-rollout numbers. I'll collect more traces tonight and draft the postmortem.

maria: thanks all. action items: @leo kernel-threshold RFC, @jasper write postmortem + KV prefetch tuning notes, @aaron patch fast_attention pin + rollout block until perf gates pass. We'll reconvene tomorrow 10:30am PT. :thumbsup:
